# Belize Travel Guide: the best things to do, see, and eat

This biodiverse nation is home to the world’s healthiest barrier reef, Mayan temples that were once the center of an ancient civilization, and lush rainforests.

![](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1018766/500x500/aa4fc68e21/author_gat_team.png/m/500x500)

by [Go Ahead Tours team](https://www.goaheadtours.com/travel-blog/authors/go-ahead-tours-team)

April 24, 2025

Nestled along the Caribbean Sea, in the northeastern corner of Central America, sits Belize, a country that beckons beachgoers, history buffs, and nature lovers. How does one country hit the travel trifecta? Well, we chatted with a Belizean Tour Director to find out. Hint: It has a little something to do with all the immersive activities on our A Week in Belize: Ruins, Reefs & Rainforests tour.

For our Belize Travel Guide, we tapped Tour Director Efrain, a Belize native and one of the experts who guides our Belize tours. “I’ve been leading EF tours for about eight years now, which has been a life-changing experience for me,” said Efrain. “I love meeting new people and sharing my country’s history, culture, and food with them.” Follow along as Efrain introduces us to the best of his country in our Belize Travel Guide.

## Belize travel basics

These fast facts will help give you the lay of the land as you dive into our Belize Travel Guide.

**Currency:** Belize dollars (BZD) is the official currency, but, “99.9% of places accept USD,” said Tour Director Efrain. He also added that you may receive change in Belize dollars (BZD), or a mix of BZD and USD. Remember: Two BZD equals one USD.

**Language:** English is the official language, but you’ll also hear Spanish, Belizean Creole, and Mayan languages like K’iche’ and Yucatec Maya.

**Location:** “This tropical wonderland is bordered to the north by Mexico, to the west and south by Guatemala, and to the east is the beautiful Caribbean Sea,” said Efrain. “We are the gateway to the Caribbean and Central America.”

**Best way to get around:** The best way to see the most sides of Belize is by driving. When you join our Belize tours, your driver will whisk from place to place via private motor coach.

[Go on a tour of Belize](https://www.goaheadtours.com/tours/north-america-tours/belize-tours)

![Ancient stone ruins surrounded by lush green trees under a blue sky, featuring a stepped pyramid-like structure and grassy hills.](https://a-us.storyblok.com/f/1018766/2688x1512/28b1ec8def/mayanruins_2688x1512.jpg/m/1536x864)

## When is the best time to visit Belize?

No Belize Travel Guide is complete without a brief intro to the weather, and what you can expect based on when you decide to visit. Spoiler alert: There will be lots of sunshine and warm temps! While it’s humid in Belize, the daily temps will shift based on where you’re staying. “Along the coast, it’s cooler, like in Belize City,” said Efrain. “Inland, it’s a little bit warmer, but I would consider Belize to have mild weather.”

### Visit in the dry season for sunny weather and outdoor exploration

Dry season in Belize runs from November through April. “To me, the best time to come to Belize is November, December, January, and February,” said Efrain. “The reason is because it’s cooler, but sunny—the sun is always shining in Belize.” Temperatures are typically in the 80s, making the weather ideal for going to the beach, snorkeling, and exploring outdoors. This dreamy weather means more travelers flock to Belize’s top attractions, so just be prepared to see more people if you visit during this peak season.

### Come in the rainy season for travel deals and fewer crowds

Rainy season, or offseason, in Belize lasts from May through October. The temperatures range from 85-90F. “Rainy season coincides with the Atlantic hurricane season, \[but Belize is not always impacted by these storms\],” said Efrain. “Around that time, we might have a tropical depression, a tropical wave, or some disturbance in the atmosphere, and we’ll get rain. When that has passed, it’s bright and the sun is shining.” If you’re willing to live with a bit of humidity and the occasional afternoon or evening shower, you’ll be rewarded in the form of lusher landscapes, lower prices, and fewer travelers at the top sites.
